It is not a separate Lean field, but each constructor hypothesis implies it: `Anchor.zero (hZ : Admissible (m:ℤ) r)` gives 3 ≤ m, 2|r| < m < m+1 and (m+1,r) ≠ (3,0); `Anchor.loop (hL : MinimalAdmissible (m+1) r) (hr : 2 ≤ |r|)` contains `Admissible (m+1) r` and forces m+1 = 2|r|+1 ≥ 5; `Anchor.loopZero (hL₀ : ((m:ℤ)+1, r) = (4,0))` gives the admissible pair (4,0). The printed spec is "on (0,ε₀) the insertion is generic and lies in one chamber". The Lean labelled-chamber conjunct is not an added hypothesis: ε ↦ softInsertion P j q ε is continuous (`continuous_softInsertion`), so once every P_ε on the connected interval (0,ε₀) is generic, its image is connected in GenericTuple and lies in one labelled chamber (take B = P_{ε₀/2}); the quotient-chamber conjunct then follows. Closest thing to a discrepancy: if "the bound of lem:soft-generic" is read as demanding all of (i)–(iv) on (0,ε₀), Lean asks only for genericity + one chamber. No discrepancy found in the four attacked encodings after expanding each to primitives and comparing with the printed words.

(1) χ_-, χ_+: def:soft prints "χ_- = -sgn det(ℓ_{j-1}, q), χ_+ = -sgn det(q, ℓ_j)" with ℓ_i = μ_{i+1} - μ_i. Lean: softAttachmentMinus P j q = -SignType.sign (det (edge P (j - 1)) q); softAttachmentPlus P j q = -SignType.sign (det q (edge P j)); edge P i = P (i+1) - P i; det u v = u.1*v.2 - u.2*v.1. Literal match. The mixed/loop sectors are taken from lem:soft-generic (iv) ("χ_- ≠ χ_+ (mixed sector)", "χ_- = χ_+ = τ (loop sector)", τ = τ_j(P)); Lean `mixed : softAttachmentMinus … ≠ softAttachmentPlus …`, `loop : softAttachmentMinus … = turn parent vertex ∧ softAttachmentPlus … = turn parent vertex`, where turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1) = sign det(P i - P (i-1), P (i+1) - P (i-1)) is τ_i of def:chirotope. The accepted rows SoftGenericLemma (lines 104-109) and SoftRotationLaw (lines 21-32) use the identical encoding, and SoftRotationLaw proves it equivalent to the cone description of lem:soft-rotation.

(2) softOldIndex j j vs "its edge E_j (from μ_j to μ_* = μ_{j+1} in the labelling of the anchor)": canonicalPosition i = ⟨(i-1).val, _⟩, boundaryIndex 0 k = k.val + 1, so softOldIndex j j = ((j-1).val + 1 : ZMod (m+1)) (theorem softOldIndex_at_attachment), i.e. the numeral j for source labels 1..m (label m ≡ 0 maps to m), and softNewIndex j = softOldIndex j j + 1 (softOldIndex_attachment_next). That is exactly the label of μ_j and of μ_* in the tuple (μ_1,…,μ_j, μ_j+εq, μ_{j+1},…,μ_n) of def:soft. The bundle's softEdge clause independently fixes the endpoints: A.polygon A.softEdge = A.parent A.vertex, A.polygon (A.softEdge + 1) = A.parent A.vertex + A.param • A.vector, edge A.polygon A.softEdge = A.param • A.vector. Faithful.

(3) MinimalAdmissible vs "(n, r) minimal": def:admissible prints "admissible if n ≥ 3, 2|r| < n and (n,r) ≠ (3,0). It is minimal if moreover n = 2|r|+1 (for r ≠ 0) or (n,r) = (4,0)". Constructor `loop (hL : MinimalAdmissible ((m : ℤ) + 1) r) (hr : 2 ≤ |r|)` = "(n, r) is minimal with |r| ≥ 2" with n = m+1.

(4) SignType.sign vs sgn: SignType.sign r for r : ℤ is 1/0/-1 exactly as sgn; the SignType→ℝ cast keeps these values, so rotationNumber parent = (r : ℝ) - (SignType.sign r : ℝ) is "rotation r − sgn(r)" and turn parent vertex = -SignType.sign r (negation in SignType) is "τ_j(P) = −sgn(r)". For |r| ≥ 2 both are ±1 as in the source.

Other clauses checked: the standing hypothesis "(n,r) admissible with n ≥ 4" is derivable from each case hypothesis (Z: Admissible m r gives m ≥ 3 and 2|r| < m < m+1; L: n = 2|r|+1 ≥ 5; L₀: (4,0)), and the three cases are mutually exclusive, so the inductive Anchor adds nothing and omits nothing. Generic parent in (L₀) is forced by the source itself ("ε₀ is the bound of lem:soft-generic", which presupposes P generic; the anchor being generic forces G1 on the triangle). bound_spec encodes the printed gloss "on (0, ε₀) the insertion is generic and lies in one chamber" (one labelled chamber and one quotient chamber, identical to clause (i) of the accepted lem:soft-generic row); I probed a stricter reading (ε₀ must witness (i)–(iv)) and found that in the mixed and loop sectors the only ε-dependent clause not fixed by chamber constancy, sgn det(u, D_ε) = τ, cannot fail before a G1 collinearity (A, M_ε, B) ends the generic interval, so no anchor-relevant weakening exists (a gap arises only in the same-sign sector, which anchors never use). Not refuted.
